speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific sensations you are experiencing with your vertigo and tell me if you noticed any accompanying hearing changes or ringing in your ears. Additionally, have you experienced any recent head trauma or severe headaches?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the brief duration of your symptoms is concerning. Have you experienced any weakness, numbness, double vision, difficulty speaking, or trouble walking since the episode? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure or recent heart issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes, absence of neurological deficits like weakness or double vision, and lack of hearing loss strongly point to BPPV rather than Meniere's or a stroke. Please try the Epley maneuver in the next hour; if symptoms persist or recur, we will perform a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
